name: Anabolic-androgenic steroid 'natty or not' evasion

lead: "Natty or not" is the online debate over whether a muscular person is drug-free. Evasion refers to concealing steroid use so that an enhanced physique is taken as natural.

For viewers, it matters because the physique shown may be set as a benchmark of what training can achieve. Many influencers avoid saying whether they are natural, which blurs the line, though more have recently begun to disclose use.

paras: This article does not cover methods of concealment. In general terms, natural federations use urinalysis or polygraph testing, while major amateur and pro leagues do not always test.
Anabolic steroid use carries documented health and legal risks. Concealment can also mislead followers about attainable results.

angle.text: This is about how physique results are perceived: concealment can make an enhanced look appear to be the product of training alone. It is not a technique for improving one's own looks.

lead: Anabolic-androgenic steroid 'natty or not' evasion refers to concealing drug use so an enhanced physique appears natural. It is part of the wider online debate over who is natural, a status that shapes how people judge what training can achieve.

Natural bodybuilding organizations formed partly in response to the cost, health risks and illegality of some steroids, and test with methods ranging from polygraph to urinalysis; the National Physique Committee does not require testing and the IFBB Pro League does not routinely test.[1] Many influencers avoid saying whether they are natural or deny being enhanced, and more recently some have disclosed use.[1]
On T Nation, a thread on the stripping of Lance Armstrong's titles includes forum members arguing whether concealing drug use in sport is cheating or common practice at elite levels.[2]

paras: Testing protocols vary by organization, as do penalties, from suspensions to permanent bans, and each keeps its own banned list.[1]
Wikipedia notes that more influencers have begun disclosing steroid use, which many see as a positive step.[1]
